claims.text: Event sourcing stores an aggregate as the ordered list of events that happened to it, instead of storing its current state as the record; the state is worked out from those events when needed.
claims.source_hint: refs/dotnet-docs/docs/architecture/ (Event Sourcing pattern); glossary event-sourcing; outline item 1

claims.text: Each aggregate's events form one event stream numbered by version (in the sample, from 1, version = position in the list); an event store only appends to the end of a stream and never updates or deletes a saved event.
claims.source_hint: glossary event-stream, event-store; examples/don-hang @ stage-3: InMemoryEventStore.cs:3-7

claims.text: At stage-3, after placing then cancelling an order, order_status_history has rows placed and cancelled and outbox_messages has order.placed and order.cancelled; the cancel sets orders.status to cancelled.
claims.source_hint: examples/don-hang @ stage-3: RecordOrderStatusHistory.cs:17-19, NotifyCustomerOnOrderEvents.cs:15-17, Entities.cs Cancel; scripts/design/order-history.sh

claims.text: order_status_history holds order_id, event, status, occurred_at; an outbox OrderMessage holds OrderId, CustomerEmail, CustomerName, OccurredAt (plus routing key); neither holds the total or the order items.

EventSourcedOrder is a sample in samples/DonHang.Samples/Samples/Design/EventSourcing; Đơn Hàng's real Order is not event-sourced and is stored by its state in orders. The sample's OrderPlaced, declared above line 74, carries CustomerId and TotalVnd.
claims.source_hint: examples/don-hang @ stage-3: EventSourcedOrder.cs:3-9; STAGE.md table row for EventSourcing/*

claims.text: EventSourcedOrder.Cancel throws InvalidOperationException if Status is cancelled or shipped, otherwise calls Record(new OrderCancelled(Id, at)); a refused change records no event.
Record calls Apply then adds the event to newEvents; Apply only sets fields (OrderCancelled sets Status cancelled) and increments Version; MarkSaved clears newEvents.
In the sample, order 5 is placed then paid: its stream holds OrderPlaced as version 1 and OrderPaid as version 2; after a cancel and Save, the stream is at version 3.
InMemoryEventStore.Save calls Append(order.Id, order.LoadedVersion, order.NewEvents) then order.MarkSaved(); Append adds events with AddRange after the existing ones (after a version check).

InMemoryEventStore keeps Dictionary<int, List<OrderEvent>> streams (one per order id; version = position) and List<OrderEvent> all; its methods are Append, ReadStream, ReadAll, Load, Save, none changes or removes an event.
The sample's comment says a real event store keeps streams in a database where a unique (stream, version) key does the version check.
claims.source_hint: examples/don-hang @ stage-3: InMemoryEventStore.cs:6-7; DECISIONS.md (outline cqrs-event-sourcing, item 2)

claims.text: OrderService loads Order from orders and changes it; it never reads order_status_history; RecordOrderStatusHistory writes the history beside orders.
NotifyCustomerOnOrderEvents builds each message as OrderMessage(order.Id, customer.Email, customer.FullName, domainEvent.OccurredAt), one per event for the six events Order records.

At stage-3 order 7, already in the repository's data, is shipped in orders and its order_status_history holds only one placed row, because the AddOrderStatusHistory migration copied only a placed row for each existing order.
Order.MarkPaid() at stage-3 sets Status to paid and records no domain event, so no outbox row and no history row follow from it.

A message in Đơn Hàng's (quorum) queues can be discarded once a consumer acknowledges (has handled) it; a queue hands messages out from its head, so it offers no way to ask for one order's events by version. Not true of RabbitMQ streams, which Đơn Hàng does not use.
claims.source_hint: RabbitMQ docs: Consumer Acknowledgements and Publisher Confirms; Quorum Queues; STAGE.md (quorum queue per service)

claims.text: The Notifications service's OrderEventsConsumer consumes from notifications.order-events (BasicConsumeAsync, then BasicAckAsync per message) and never asks for an order's earlier messages.

scripts/design/event-sourcing.sh runs on the host with dotnet run --project samples/DonHang.Samples -- event-sourcing; its output starts with the stream of order 5 (version 1 OrderPlaced at 09:00, version 2 OrderPaid at 09:30) and a line 'A cancels and appends: the stream is now at version 3'.
Decide whether a system is event-sourced by what it loads as the truth: a history kept beside a state row is a read model, not event sourcing, even when it lists every change.
